newsitem.title: USA: Fund mgr Davis sees 'dangerous' investor euphoria.
newsitem.headline: Fund mgr Davis sees 'dangerous' investor euphoria.

text.p: Unconcerned about a bear market for U.S. stocks in the near term, the portfolio manager of the popular Selected American Shares Fund instead worries that investor "euphoria" could drive the Dow Industrials to a "dangerous" level of 9,000-10,000 points in the next 12 months.

"There's an upside blowoff that could happen anytime," Shelby Davis told Reuters in an interview before speaking at a Charles Schwab & Co Inc conference here on Friday. "You could look to the euphoria enveloping the market as dangerous."
The Dow Industrials could add 3,000 or 4,000 points if investor euphoria gets out of control, said Davis, who was billed by Schwab as one of the industry's "legendary" managers.

Davis sees no reason to expect a bear market anytime soon, and said that macroeconomic and corporate conditions exist to allow for a continuing bull market. He cited good earnings prospects and market confidence.
"A bull market is climbing the wall of worry," he said.
Sectors that he likes include financial services, which he feels is overvalued and will benefit as more individuals focus on retirement and other investments.
He sees the stocks as undervalued. Favorites include SunAmerica, Travelers Group, and Schwab.

Another popular segment is oil services, which will continue to benefit from consolidation and close attention to expense control by the oil giants. He cites Schlumberger Ltd and Halliburton as favorites.
The $1.2 billion fund has a cash position of five percent, and is committed to be fully invested in mostly American stocks, he said.

Davis tends to hold stocks for three years, and likens the fund to a ocean liner. "We're a ship setting across the ocean," he said. "We're going to hit sunny days and stormy days, and we're just committed to getting across the ocean."
Among the top holdings are American Express Co, Wells Fargo and Co, Intel Corp, Travelers, Allstate Corp, and Citicorp.
Year to date, the fund is up 25.5 percent, compared to the S&P 500 index up 18.14 percent, and is up 15.5 percent annually over a five-year time frame.
